regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like acceleration — but IIP YoY slipped to 6.7% from 8.8%, core sector eased to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%, and PMI manufacturing fell to 52.8 from 53.5. The composite PMI at 54.6 is being carried by services, not goods. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is encouraging, but the inversion is this: if goods-producing sectors are losing momentum while services hold, the growth quality is narrowing — and services-led growth is harder to sustain when real wages are being eroded by 22.93% YoY fuel inflation.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY understates the pressure: fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) is feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY, and the RBI has already revised its own forecast up 50bps to 5.1% YoY. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY appears contained — but that gap between core and headline is the trapdoor. When fuel costs transmit into logistics and manufacturing input costs with a one-to-two quarter lag, core will follow. The RBI is watching a number that has not yet moved; the number that has moved is already at a near-record.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY — a 630bps divergence — keeps the CD ratio at 81.4% (75th percentile historically). Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month is at its lowest on record (0th percentile), meaning capital markets are not providing the relief valve. The historical analogue is instructive: the last time the CD ratio sustained above 80% during a rate-pause cycle, the RBI responded with macro-prudential tightening on risk weights within two to three quarters. NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% suggests the wholesale funding pressure is migrating, not dissipating.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. with RBI's own inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY leaves a real rate of approximately 15bps — thin enough to be irrelevant as an anchor. The RBI is on pause, but the bond market is not: US 10Y at 5.18% yield is tightening global financial conditions regardless of what Mint Street decides. The second-order effect: if INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) continues to weaken, imported inflation feeds back into CPI with a two-quarter lag, forcing the RBI's hand not on growth grounds but on currency defence grounds — a rate hike cycle nobody is pricing.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity from 75.6% is the most credible signal in today's data — 77% is the empirical threshold above which private capex becomes self-reinforcing. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (up from 6.5%) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (up from 10.2%) confirm that financing is flowing. The inversion: core sector growth at 5.4% YoY, moderating from 6.0%, suggests the upstream inputs to capex — steel, cement, electricity — are not accelerating in lockstep. Watch whether core sector re-accelerates in the next print before declaring the capex cycle self-sustaining.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month and passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY alongside two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY signal broad consumption strength — but the GST number demands decomposition. At ₹1,99,853 cr, it is at the 71st percentile, not a record, and the FYTD figure of ₹10,42,757 cr sits at only the 14th percentile, suggesting the monthly print is partly seasonal or advance-filing driven. Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY are the more reliable rural demand proxy — and they are strong. The divergence to watch: if urban discretionary (PV sales, airline passengers at 86.4 mn / month) stays elevated while rural credit (agriculture credit at 17% YoY) is being pulled forward, the consumption story may be borrowing from future quarters.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) remains elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY prior) signals wholesale funding pressure. Corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month (at 0th percentile — lowest on record) indicates capital markets are not absorbing the overflow.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and refinancing risk. RBI will likely ease liquidity via OMOs or CRR cuts within 2-3 months if deposit growth doesn't accelerate. Position for a 25-50 bps rate cut by Q3 FY27.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile has historically preceded either deposit acceleration or RBI policy easing. Last time CD ratio was this elevated (2022), RBI cut rates 250 bps over 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) signals robust investment demand. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month, at 74th percentile) is at the inflection point where capex becomes self-reinforcing. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior) is moderating but remains positive. India's FY27 GDP forecast at 7.7% YoY (at 80th percentile — highest in 10 years) reflects capex-led growth expectations. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (up from 6.5% prior) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (up from 10.2% prior) confirm broad-based capex financing.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Increase exposure to project-linked equities (L&T, Larsen & Toubro, Godrej & Boyce). Capex cycle typically runs 18-24 months; we are in month 8-10 of this upcycle. Expect order book visibility to remain strong through FY27. Avoid defensive sectors; rotation into cyclicals is justified.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the 74th percentile; historically, sustained capex cycles begin when CU exceeds 75%. This is the early-to-mid stage of a multi-year investment cycle.","is_surprise":false}

SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (up from 18.21 ₹ lakh cr, rising 2 consecutive months, at 93rd percentile). SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn, at 82nd percentile). MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (rising 2 consecutive months, at 86th percentile). DII equity net flows at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (up from 35,099 ₹ cr net / month, at 100th percentile — all-time high). This level has historically coincided with market peaks (2021) and troughs (2020); current context suggests mid-cycle strength.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY, at 95th percentile — near-record high). WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78% YoY). Brent crude at 97.47 $/bbl (flat, at 69th percentile). WTI at 92.44 $/bbl (flat, at 78th percentile). Natural gas at 3.251 $/MMBtu (at 20th percentile — historically low, but up from 2.83 $/MMBtu 2 months prior). CPI headline at 4.45% YoY (up from 4.38% YoY, at 41st percentile). RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (up from 4.6% YoY).","implication":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a structural headwind for RBI's rate-cut cycle. Even if core inflation moderates, headline CPI will remain sticky above 4.5% through Q2 FY27 due to fuel base effects. This delays RBI's easing window by 1-2 months. Hedge long-duration bond positions; 10-year yields will likely stay elevated at 5.8-6.0% until fuel inflation rolls over. Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) as a hedge against further oil price spikes.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is the highest in the past decade outside of 2022 (post-Ukraine spike). This level has historically forced RBI to maintain a hawkish bias for 2-3 quarters.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Pause Masks Tightening Bias Globally","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.63% p.a. (flat, at 67th percentile mid). US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.18% yield (up from 5.11%, at 94th percentile — near-record high). Fed balance sheet at 6,746.548 $ bn (rising 3 in a row, at 47th percentile). BOJ rate at 1% p.a. (up from 0.75% p.a., at 86th percentile — highest in 10 years). ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. This level has historically coincided with EM capital outflows and currency depreciation.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakens as Carry Unwinds Accelerate","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 ₹ (up from 95.8 ₹, at 91st percentile — near-record weak). INR has depreciated 90 paise in 5 months (95.24 → 96.15). FII equity net flows at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month, but volatile: -114 → -3,111.9 → +29,631 over 3 months). India VIX at 12.16 index (falling 5 in a row, at 7th percentile — complacency signal).","implication":"INR weakness at 96.15 ₹/$ reflects both BOJ tightening (carry unwind) and FII volatility. Monitor FII flows closely — if they turn negative for 2 consecutive months, INR could breach 97 ₹/$.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness is the weakest in the current cycle. This level has historically preceded RBI intervention and temporary stabilisation, but not reversal.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Collapse Masks GCC Real Estate Shift","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (down from 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter, at 6th percentile — near-record low). Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (down from 16.1% vacant, at 42nd percentile). Retail mall vacancy at 5% vacant (down from 7.5% vacant, at 8th percentile, at 84th percentile signal strength). Nifty IT index flat YTD while office absorption has collapsed 50% from peak (48 mn sq ft / quarter in Q3 FY26 → 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter now). Yet, Bengaluru office rents at 100 ₹/sqft/mo (stable) and Mumbai rents at 126 ₹/sqft/mo (up from 121.5 ₹/sqft/mo). Retail mall vacancy at 5% (lowest in 10 years) while office vacancy at 14.5% (elevated).","implication":"Traditional IT services are NOT the marginal buyer of office space anymore. Global Capability Centers (GCCs) — captive R&D centers of multinational corporates — are the new marginal buyer. GCCs are smaller, more selective, and concentrated in Bengaluru/Hyderabad. This explains why office absorption has collapsed while rents remain stable (supply-demand mismatch by micro-location). Retail mall strength (5% vacancy) reflects e-commerce logistics hubs and experiential retail, not traditional retail. IMPLICATION: Overweight commercial real estate plays with GCC-focused portfolios (Embassy, Mindspace). Avoid generic office REITs with legacy IT tenant concentration. This is a structural shift in India's real estate demand — IT services are no longer the growth engine; GCCs and logistics are.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile is near-record low, but this masks a compositional shift. GCC demand is stable; IT services demand is collapsing. Retail mall vacancy at 8th percentile (lowest in 10 years) signals a structural reallocation of real estate capital away from traditional office to experiential/logistics.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry Growth — Goods Economy Quietly Fades

The facts:

  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) — but PMI Manufacturing fell to 52.8 from 53.5 while Services rose to 54.5 from 53.3; goods momentum is reversing.
  • IIP YoY slowed to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%; core sector eased to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% — upstream industrial signals contradict the composite headline.
  • Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) is the one unambiguous positive — above the threshold where private capex becomes self-reinforcing.
  • But two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY and PV sales at 16% YoY suggest consumption is holding — the question is whether it is demand or credit-pull.

The tension: GDP at 7.8% YoY is accelerating on paper; the goods economy — IIP, core sector, manufacturing PMI — is decelerating in practice. Services and consumption are carrying a load that industrial output is not confirming.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY in the next print: a third consecutive deceleration below 5% YoY would signal the goods economy is diverging structurally from the headline.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

Equity All-Time Highs — Bond Market Prices the Reckoning

The facts:

  • Nikkei 225 at 66,364 (100th percentile) and Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,303 (100th percentile) — both at all-time highs, pricing synchronised global expansion.
  • But US 10Y Treasury at 5.18% yield (94th percentile, up from 5.11%) is tightening real financial conditions faster than any central bank rate decision.
  • US GDP SAAR slowed to 1.5% SAAR from 2.1%; China GDP at 4.3% YoY from 5.0% with PMI Composite at 49.5 — the two largest economies are decelerating.
  • BOJ rate at 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile, highest in 10 years) — yen carry unwind is the underappreciated transmission mechanism into EM equity flows.

The tension: Global equities are at all-time highs; global growth is slowing and bond yields are near decade highs. One of these is wrong — and the bond market has a better forecasting record.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.0% p.a. is the tail risk for India liquidity: any further hike accelerates yen carry unwind and pressures FII equity flows, which are already volatile (₹-114 cr → ₹29,631 cr net / month in three months).

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record — Deposit Gap Caps the Ceiling

The facts:

  • DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile, all-time high) — domestic institutional absorption is at a level that has historically cushioned FII volatility.
  • SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile, rising two consecutive months); SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile).
  • But bank credit at 17.1% YoY vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY — a 630bps gap — keeps the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile).
  • Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (0th percentile — lowest on record) means the capital market relief valve is closed; NBFC credit accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals wholesale funding migration.

The tension: Equity liquidity is at all-time highs; credit liquidity is structurally strained. The two pools are not connected — strong SIP flows do not fund bank deposits, and the deposit gap is not narrowing.

Bottom line: If deposit growth does not recover toward 13% YoY within two quarters, macro-prudential tightening via risk weights on unsecured lending becomes the base case, not the tail risk.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Demand Holds Premium — Office REITs Price the Absorption Collapse

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up from 15%, +5 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $135.46 bn (14% YoY) sustain the bid.
  • Launch mix skewed to premium and above: luxury (₹1.5–2.5 cr) at 25% of supply and ultra-luxury (>₹2.5 cr) at 22% — but sales momentum is negative in MMR (-8% YoY), NCR (-6% YoY), and Pune (-15% YoY).
  • Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (6th percentile) — GCC occupiers at 42% of leasing are holding rents stable (Bengaluru ₹100/sqft/mo, Mumbai ₹126/sqft/mo) even as aggregate volumes collapse.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down sharply from prior prints — the equity market is pricing the absorption weakness, not the rent stability.
  • Bank Nifty at 55,580 (92nd percentile) — near all-time highs despite the CD ratio stress — is the equity market's most visible complacency signal.

The tension: NRI demand and GCC leasing are holding the premium and office rent floors; but residential sales volumes are falling in five of seven cities and REIT unit prices are declining. The floor is real; the ceiling is not.

Bottom line: Overweight premium residential in NRI-favoured cities (MMR, Bengaluru, Hyderabad) on NRI bid; avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 20 mn sq ft / quarter.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Sequencing Is Everything

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) — if Brent holds above $95/bbl, WPI-to-CPI passthrough forces RBI's inflation forecast above 5.5% YoY, closing the rate-cut window entirely.
  • US 10Y at 5.18% yield (94th percentile, rising) — every 25bps further tightens global financial conditions, pressures INR at 96.15 (91st percentile), and risks FII reversal from the current ₹29,631 cr net / month.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits with corporate bond issuance at a record-low ₹18,700 cr / month — if deposit growth does not recover, macro-prudential tightening on NBFC risk weights is the regulatory response.
  • India VIX at 12.16 (7th percentile, falling five consecutive sessions) — historically, sub-12 VIX precedes sharp corrections; complacency is priced in at precisely the moment global tail risks are rising.

The tension: Each risk is manageable in isolation; the danger is sequencing — a US 10Y spike triggers INR weakness, which feeds fuel inflation, which forces RBI tightening, which hits the CD ratio stress simultaneously.

Bottom line: Watch US 10Y Treasury this week: a close above 5.25% yield would reprice India rate-cut expectations, pressure INR, and likely trigger the first meaningful FII equity outflow since July.

"}
